A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EvoMAS work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, query-order experiments, and analyses of evolved configurations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds budget-controlled comparisons, further ablations, and AIME evaluation.

M1.justification: The core configuration representation, evolutionary operators, and pool/memory framework are retained. However, new Appendix C.3 specifies stochastic mutation/crossover selection with probabilities 0.8/0.2, whereas v1 Appendix D.3 and retained v3 Appendix E.3 describe choices driven by the meta-model and evolution stage. The PDFs do not resolve whether the procedure changed or the implementation account conflicts with the retained narrative.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on 60 AIME 2024–2025 competition mathematics problems (Appendix A.17, Table 23). This extends mathematical reasoning coverage while retaining the original BBEH, BBEH-Mini, WorkBench, and SWE-Bench evaluations.

E2.justification: v3 evaluates ARG-Designer and AFlow on BBEH-Mini (Tables 21–22), and adds mini-SWE-agent/SWE-agent looping and SWE-agent Best-of-6/10 comparisons on SWE-Bench-Verified (Table 15). These substantially expand the empirical comparator set. MASS appears only in the conceptual comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include token-budget controls using looping with pass@N and judge-selected Best-of-N, meta-model variation with a fixed agent-model pool, judge agreement against ground truth, and controls disabling pool updates or memory. These extend evaluation design; the original benchmark sizes and sequential evaluation protocol remain.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the original pool/depth, reward, transfer, and ordering analyses, v3 adds cost decomposition, budget controls, beta sensitivity, separate meta-model and judge ablations, pool/memory contribution analysis, and perturbed or agent-generated initialization tests (Appendices A.8–A.14). These investigate substantial previously untested explanations and sensitivities.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent trials per query and the same 11 query-order shuffles, including standard deviation 1.1%. v3 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the corresponding original appendix result tables retain their numerical results. v3 adds substantial result sets: for example, 42.7% resolution at 29M tokens versus Best-of-10's 37.8% at 40M tokens (Table 15), 40.4% without accumulation versus 49.1% with both components (Table 19), and 56.7% on AIME versus Peer Review's 51.7% (Table 23).

T1.justification: Section 3.2.3 newly specifies the previously abstract cost term as Cost(C)=T+1000L, defining token usage and latency contributions. The configuration definition and existing evolutionary equations otherwise remain, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract's scientific claims and the introduction's three principal contributions remain essentially unchanged. The conclusion adds an explicit applicability qualification: EvoMAS targets settings prioritizing accuracy over latency, with reducing evolution cost identified as future work.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning the independent value of per-query evolution, complementary benefits of pool and memory, judge robustness through detectable execution failures, and amortization of evolution costs. It also explicitly discusses the accuracy–latency tradeoff. The earlier transfer interpretations and configuration failure cases remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access statement, explicit cost scaling and default beta, retrieval of up to three experiences, and an implementation appendix describing parent selection, operator probabilities, single-call operators, validation, and fallback behavior. Per-query token/time breakdowns further document resource requirements. These are newly reported details, not evidence that all underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix A.18 substantially expand positioning against MASS, ARG-Designer, and AFlow. New Table 24 contrasts optimization targets, joint evolution, cross-query learning, and inference-time adaptation, explicitly positioning EvoMAS as uniquely combining these capabilities. Bibliographic corrections are separate from this substantive expansion.

P1.justification: v3 expands methodological explanations, condenses and reorganizes Sections 4.4–5, and inserts an implementation appendix before the retained prompts and examples. Author ordering, publication text, disclosure, and cross-references also change. The introduction and most existing appendix prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 introduces main-text summary tables for ablations, mutation patterns, and budget comparisons, plus appendix tables covering costs, robustness, additional comparators, AIME, and method characteristics. Existing figures and detailed tables are retained, with several relocated. The expanded tabular presentation is substantive beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added budget and accumulation controls address v1's limited separation of evolutionary benefits from compute and memory reuse, while implementation and code-access documentation improve auditability. The gain is qualified by new inconsistencies: Table 2's default T=1 scores of 44.4/45.4 conflict with retained Table 12's 45.2/46.2, and Appendix C.3's fixed operator probabilities conflict with Appendix E.3's adaptive-choice account. These issues limit the reliability of the expanded explanations.
